BoxData.description: A box - a pure container. It never renders inline text; nest a `Text` child for that.

parent_id.description: Index into the `Vec<UiNode>` of this node's parent; `None` = root.

selected.description:
0 = none, 1 = secondary, 2 = primary/active. The renderer owns how it's drawn - it must
NOT overload `border_*` to signal selection.

squircle.description:
`true` renders corners as a superellipse ("squircle") instead of a circular arc, at
the same `corner_radius`. Box-shadow blur always stays circular-arc regardless - see
`BoxShadow`'s own doc note.

BoxExtra.description:
Extended flex/grid layout properties, grouped so `BoxData` needn't name every field. Every
field is optional - an absent `extra` is all-defaults.

align_content.description:
Container-level `align-content` - distribution of extra space among grid tracks on the
block axis. `None` = taffy default (Stretch). Distinct from `align_items`, which
positions a track's own content within the track.

align_items.description: Cross-axis alignment of children (`align-items`). `None` = taffy default (Stretch).

flex_basis.description: `flex-basis`. `None` = `auto`; a "Fill" item wants `Px(0)` for a pure share of free space.

gap.description: Uniform gap between children (`gap`), flex and grid.

grid_template_areas.description: `grid-template-areas` - named regions, resolved to numeric line coordinates.

justify_items.description:
Container-level `justify-items` (grid's inline-axis default for items). `None` = taffy
default (Stretch). No flex analog - flex has no separate justify-items concept.

justify_self.description: Per-item `justify-self` override - the grid analog of `align_self` on the inline axis.

BoxShadow.description:
A drop shadow (`box-shadow`). Always blurs against a circular-arc corner, even when the
owning `BoxData`/`TextData.squircle` is `true` - an exact squircle blur has no closed form
(would need a 2D numeric quadrature over the implicit boundary); this is an accepted,
deliberate visual inconsistency (rounded shadow under a sharp squircle corner), not a bug.

Deform.description:
The shared `p -> p'` deformation contract (`resources/foundation.md` Pillar C): one
vocabulary consumed by text Stage C glyph placement, SDF domain warp (future Pillar E),
MotionPath, DrawSVG, and MorphSVG, so none of them grows a private warp system. `None` on
the field that carries this (e.g. `TextData.deform`) means identity - existing scenes stay
byte-identical.

Only `ArclengthPath` is consumed anywhere today (Vellum's text-on-path, `text.md` Phase 2).
The other variants are the reserved shape of this contract for Pillar E
(`resources/sdf3d.md`) and are not yet interpreted by any renderer - additive, inert until
driven, same posture as every other not-yet-consumed wire variant in this dialect.

Each variant carries a Lipschitz tier note (`sdf3d.md` §1, §4): a surface warp preserves
the distance metric and a raymarcher can step through it normally; a space warp breaks the
bound and must shrink its step size. That tier is part of a variant's contract, not an
afterthought, even before Pillar E has a raymarcher to enforce it.

oneOf.description:
A plain 2D affine, `[a, b, c, d, e, f]` (the standard SVG/Canvas row-major convention:
`x' = a*x + c*y + e`, `y' = b*x + d*y + f`). Distance-preserving (surface-tier).

Bind to an arc-length-parameterized path: `points` is a polyline in the deformed
node's own local coordinate space (same origin/units as `ShapeKind::Path`'s segments -
the node's own box), walked at constant speed by length rather than by raw parameter.
`offset` is an arc-length offset (same units as `points`) added before parameterizing,
so an animated/authored offset can slide content along the path without re-deriving
it. Distance-preserving (surface-tier) off the path itself.

2D -> 2D bound to a deformed quad (four corners), a la "envelope distort" /
Illustrator's "Make with Warp". Reserved for Pillar E - shape only, unconsumed.

Project onto an SDF/mesh surface (`text.md` §7's "text on a surface", route a).
Reserved for Pillar E - shape only, unconsumed.

A space warp (twist / bend / displace), `sdf3d.md` §4's domain-warp family. Breaks the
Lipschitz bound (space-tier) - a raymarch consumer must shrink its step size. Reserved
for Pillar E - shape only, unconsumed.

Extent.description:
A box-model size dimension (mirrors taffy's `Dimension`). `fr` is deliberately absent -
fractional-of-free-space is a container concern (`TrackSize::Fr` / flex grow), not a size a
child declares about itself.

oneOf.description: Size to content / fill per flex-grow.

Fraction of the parent's definite size (`0.5` == `50%`); resolves to `Auto` under an
auto-sized parent (standard CSS percentage behavior).

FillRule.description:
Which fill values count as "inside" a `ShapeKind::Path` contour. Mirrors
`fdsm::bezier::scanline::FillRule`'s variant set exactly (same names, same order), so a
renderer's Path-baking code can map this 1:1 with no translation table.

FlexDir.description:
CSS `flex-direction`. Previously emitted as a bare `String` by Charter - now a real enum, so
an invalid value fails to deserialize instead of silently mismatching.

GridLine.description:
A grid line reference for item placement. Not `Copy` - `NamedLine`/`NamedSpan` carry an
owned name, unlike every other variant.

oneOf.description:
`span <name>` - spans until the nth line with this name (mirrors taffy's own
`GridPlacement::NamedSpan`, which also carries a count).

GridTemplateArea.description:
One named `grid-template-areas` region, resolved to numeric line coordinates (mirrors
taffy's own `GridTemplateArea`). `row_start`/`column_start` are 1-indexed grid lines;
`row_end`/`column_end` are exclusive (one past the area's last line), matching
`grid-row`/`grid-column`'s own end-line convention.

ImageSource.description: Where an image's pixels come from. `Ref` names a previously-loaded image by id.

extra.description:
Flex/grid-item participation, same as `TextData.extra` - see its own doc comment.
Unlike Text, Img's min/max above ARE meaningful (Img reads its authored width/height
for real), so this one gets the full sizing treatment.

opacity.description:
Node-level multiplier, same meaning as `BoxData.opacity`/`ShapeData.opacity` - composes
with each instance's own `opacity` (see the dynamic-layer doc comments on those
fields). Defaults to `1.0`, not `0.0` (a bare `#[serde(default)]` would make every
already-saved image invisible) - every other `ImgData` field below `object_position`
predates this one and is `#[serde(default)]`-tolerant for exactly this reason.

padding.description:
`Img`'s own paint properties, same shape as `TextData`'s (reuses the same
`extract_paint_props`-style helper on the interpreter side) - a framed/highlighted
image doesn't need a wrapper Box any more than a highlighted text label does.

NodePosition.description:
CSS `position`, with `inset` folded into the offset-carrying variants (only meaningful
there). `Relative` participates in normal flow, unshifted - the default.

`Nudged { dx, dy }` is the CSS `position: relative; top/left` analog: stays a full
participant of the parent's flex/grid flow (siblings and the parent's own auto-sizing are
computed as if this node were unshifted), but its final PAINTED rect - and its whole
subtree's - is translated by `(dx, dy)`. Pure post-layout, paint-time offset; never touches
a renderer's real layout-engine `Position`/`inset` machinery, same discipline as the other
two offset variants below.

`Absolute { x, y }` floats the node at a world-space offset, unrelated to any parent - see
the renderer's own docs (e.g. taf_can_do's TECHNICAL.md) for why placement is decoupled
from sizing here (a real CSS `Position::Absolute` couples "leave flow" with shrink-to-fit
sizing, which collapses text to zero width). Root-only by construction in every consumer
today (an interpreter only ever sets this on a view nothing else's composition references).

`Anchored { dx, dy }` is a parent-relative sibling of `Absolute`: also leaves the immediate
parent's flex/grid flow (consumes no sibling space, sized independently via ordinary
auto-sizing - never a real Position::Absolute either), but resolves against that PARENT's
own resolved rect instead of world space (`parent.position + (dx, dy)`). The "badge pinned
to a card's corner" case `Absolute` can't express, since `Absolute` has no parent
relationship at all. A renderer resolves `Anchored` only after its recorded parent's own
rect is known; a node whose PARENT is itself `Anchored` conservatively falls back to
`Relative` (no concrete use case yet for chained anchoring - see the renderer's own docs).

OklabColor.description:
Oklab color, the internal + wire representation (never sRGB). Authored as OKLCH, stored as
`(l, a, b, alpha)`. `Default` is fully transparent (`alpha = 0`).

PathSegment.description:
One Bezier segment of a `ShapeKind::Path` contour, in the shape's own local coordinate
space (same origin/units as the containing `ShapeData`'s box). Mirrors
`fdsm::bezier::Segment`'s three constructible orders (`line`/`quad`/`cubic`) exactly, so a
renderer's Path-baking code can map each variant onto the matching `fdsm` constructor with
no reinterpretation.

ShapeData.description:
A parametric vector shape (rect / ellipse / line / regular polygon / star), rendered via an
analytic SDF rather than a rasterized quad. Sized like `Box` (mirrors its width/height/min/max
so Fixed/Hug/Fill resizing and flex/grid participation work identically); `hug` has no
intrinsic content to hug, so it behaves like an explicit size. Fill/stroke are ordinary
resolvable properties, never baked - same as every other paintable property in this dialect.

selected.description: 0 = none, 1 = secondary, 2 = primary/active - same convention as `BoxData.selected`.

ShapeKind.description:
The geometric kind of a `Shape` node, and its shape-specific parameters. `Path` (Phase 2,
freeform) is an arbitrary boundary authored as a flat list of segments - never a brush or
pressure concept, just geometry a plugin has already computed (see
resources/vellum-sprite-batch-plan.md). Scoped to `closed: true` for v1; an unfilled
open-path stroke render is a deferred, separate concern.

TextAlign.description: CSS `text-align` (LTR-relative; no bidi yet). `Left` is the wire default.

TextData.description: A text run. Always declares `Auto` size; the renderer measures it during layout.

deform.description:
The shared Pillar C deformation contract - only `Deform::ArclengthPath` (text-on-path)
is interpreted today. `None` = identity, byte-identical to every scene before this
field existed.

extra.description:
Flex/grid-item participation (align-self, grid-column/row, margin, position) - lets a
Text node be a real grid item or set align-self without a wrapper Box. Deliberately no
min/max width/height companion fields the way `BoxData`/`ShapeData`/`SpriteBatchData`
have: Text's width/height are hardcoded `Auto` regardless of authored props (the
renderer measures it), so a min/max clamp would have no effect - don't add one without
also giving Text real sizing to clamp.

line_height.description: Absolute px; `<= 0.0` means "not provided" (renderer falls back to a ratio).

squircle.description:
Same superellipse-corner toggle as `BoxData.squircle` - `Text` paints its own
background/border/radius via the shared `extract_paint_props` helper.

TextDecorationKind.description: CSS `text-decoration`, single-choice (never underline AND line-through at once).

TrackMax.description: The upper bound of a `minmax()` track - same shapes as `TrackMin` plus `Fr`.

TrackMin.description:
The lower bound of a `minmax()` track - CSS `<track-breadth>` minus `fr`, since a min bound
can never itself be a flex fraction.

TrackSize.description: A single CSS grid track size.

oneOf.description:
`repeat(auto-fit, minmax(<f32>px, 1fr))` - the one responsive-grid shape the Grid
arrangement needs, not a general `repeat()`.
`<f32>%` of the grid container's own definite size.

`repeat(auto-fill, minmax(<f32>px, 1fr))` - `AutoFit`'s sibling: fills as many tracks as
fit without collapsing/stretching empty ones into existing content, CSS's real
auto-fit-vs-auto-fill distinction.
Arbitrary `minmax(<min>, <max>)`, for a shape none of the fixed variants above cover.
